data.name: Blight of the Immortals
data.detailed_description:
Fantasy! Strategy! Zombies!

A plague of undead creatures threatens to overwhelm the land and with the fall of each town to the Blight, more walking dead rise and the zombie apocalypse draws nearer.


For the first time in centuries, the six great races of Alundria must stand together. The lawful races of Elves, Dwarves, and Men; and the chaotic races of Orcs, Goblins, and Trolls. The strengths that make each race unique... magic, money, and might are twisted and darkened as each creature returns from the dead as a zombie version of its former self.

To save the world, you must recruit heroes, expand your empire, and raise armies as fast as you can because as time marches on, so does the zombie horde.

Features

  • Blight is a unique blend of Online Strategy Board game and Collectible Card Game.

  • Multiplayer is Co-OP. Players must work together to defeat the zombies.

  • Multiplayer is slow-real-time and always ticking away in the background. There is no need to wait for your turn, simply login throughout the day to command your forces and coordinate with the other players.

  • In Single Player is turn-based and you can choose how far ahead in time to jump each turn. Earn Valour by throwing caution to the wind and jumping ahead 12 hours or pay Valour to micromanage your forces and jump ahead just 1 hour.

  • The Single Player campaign include 36 missions spanning the 6 different races. Explore new strategies, collect new hero cards, and master the different races with each new scenario.

  • Collect over 100 Hero Cards and explore new strategies and combinations with each deck you build.

Early Access


Help us test this Early Access build and let us know whats working and whats not. We love hearing from our community and so please join us and be a part of the game's development!

About Iron Helmet

Iron Helmet is the developer behind the award-winning strategy game, Neptune's Pride. Named PC Gamer's Webgame of the Year, Runner Up to Edge Magazine's Indie Game of the Year, and Honourable Mention in the IGF Grand Prize category.

Iron Helmet is Jay Kyburz and Penny Sweetser, who have worked on AAA titles such as BioShock, BioShock 2, Total War, Tribes, Freedom Force, and SWAT 4.

reviews.review:
Blight of the Immortals presents an intriguing combination of fantasy warfare, strategic territory management, collectible hero cards, and cooperative survival against an expanding undead invasion. Developed and published by Iron Helmet Games, this free-to-play strategy title distinguishes itself through its emphasis on calculated decisions rather than rapid combat. Set in the fantasy world of Alundria, the game challenges players to unite opposing civilizations against a supernatural plague that transforms fallen populations into additional enemies. Its combination of board game mechanics and persistent strategic threats creates an experience that rewards patience, preparation, and careful resource allocation. Although its presentation is relatively modest, the underlying systems provide an appealing challenge for players who enjoy complex strategic planning.

The game's central conflict revolves around six playable races: Elves, Dwarves, Men, Orcs, Goblins, and Trolls. Each civilization brings different strengths to the battlefield, encouraging players to adapt their tactics according to their chosen faction. Some races offer advantages in economic development or magical capabilities, while others emphasize military effectiveness. This diversity becomes especially important because the undead threat grows stronger whenever settlements fall. Rather than simply conquering territory, players must consider how every offensive or defensive decision influences the survival of the entire region. Losing an important settlement can create additional dangers, making reckless expansion particularly risky.

The strategic gameplay focuses on recruiting armies, controlling territories, strengthening defenses, and confronting increasingly dangerous undead forces. What makes these activities engaging is the constant pressure created by the spreading Blight. Enemies cannot simply be ignored while players concentrate on economic growth, since delaying action may allow the undead to overwhelm neighboring settlements. Successful campaigns require balancing immediate military needs with longer-term development. This creates satisfying moments when carefully coordinated attacks succeed, but it can also become frustrating when earlier mistakes lead to overwhelming enemy advantages. Players who appreciate meaningful consequences will likely enjoy this demanding structure.

Another distinctive feature is the collectible hero card system, which introduces additional customization into the traditional strategy formula. With more than 100 hero cards available, players can experiment with combinations that complement their preferred approaches. These cards contribute to strategic flexibility and encourage experimentation across different scenarios. Instead of relying entirely on numerical military superiority, players must consider how individual abilities interact with their overall objectives. This system adds depth and replayability, although newcomers may initially find the number of available options intimidating. Understanding effective combinations requires experimentation, and some strategies may prove considerably more efficient than others.

The single-player campaign offers 36 missions distributed across the six races, providing opportunities to explore different tactical possibilities. One particularly inventive mechanic involves controlling how quickly time advances. Players can progress through larger time intervals to earn Valour or spend that resource to advance more cautiously in smaller increments. This creates an interesting balance between efficiency and precision. Advancing too quickly risks overlooking developing threats, while excessive caution consumes resources that might prove valuable later. The mechanic gives players meaningful control over the rhythm of their campaigns and reinforces the importance of anticipating consequences rather than reacting impulsively.

Cooperative multiplayer takes a different approach from conventional real-time strategy games by allowing participants to coordinate their actions asynchronously. Players do not necessarily need to remain connected simultaneously, making it possible to manage campaigns over extended periods. This design accommodates individuals with limited gaming time while encouraging communication and coordinated planning. However, its effectiveness depends heavily on the reliability of participating players. Inconsistent cooperation can slow progress or disrupt important strategies. Those accustomed to immediate multiplayer action may find the pacing unusually restrained, but players who enjoy persistent strategic campaigns may appreciate this flexibility.

Visually, the game favors clarity and functionality over elaborate graphical effects. Its fantasy environments, territorial maps, and unit representations communicate the essential information needed for strategic decision-making. The presentation reflects its board game influences, emphasizing mechanical depth rather than cinematic spectacle. While this approach suits the experience, it also makes the game appear less polished than many contemporary strategy titles. The atmosphere is established primarily through its fantasy setting and escalating undead threat rather than detailed animations or dramatic storytelling. Players seeking impressive graphics or immersive battlefield action may therefore find the visual experience underwhelming.

The learning curve represents another potential obstacle. Although the objective of defeating the undead is straightforward, mastering faction abilities, hero combinations, economic management, and time advancement requires considerable attention. Beginners may struggle to identify which threats demand immediate intervention, particularly when several settlements face simultaneous attacks. Nevertheless, this complexity contributes to the game's long-term appeal. Successfully overcoming difficult scenarios through improved planning can feel genuinely rewarding, especially when previously unsuccessful strategies are refined into effective solutions.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently listed as Unknown, meaning Valve has not officially classified the game as Verified, Playable, or Unsupported. Its relatively simple visual presentation may reduce hardware demands, but interface readability, mouse-oriented controls, and online account requirements remain potential concerns. Consequently, smooth handheld performance cannot be guaranteed without further testing.

Overall, Blight of the Immortals offers an unconventional and intellectually stimulating strategy experience that successfully combines fantasy warfare, collectible cards, and an evolving undead threat. Its greatest strengths are its meaningful tactical decisions, diverse factions, flexible time management, and cooperative possibilities. However, its slow pacing, basic visuals, demanding mechanics, and reliance on dependable multiplayer participants prevent it from appealing equally to everyone. For dedicated strategy enthusiasts who value careful planning over immediate action, it remains an interesting and worthwhile experience.

A thoughtfully designed fantasy strategy game with substantial tactical depth and distinctive mechanics, best suited to patient players who enjoy challenging campaigns and methodical decision-making.

Rating: 7/10
